records.current_summary:
Arica y Parinacota is grouped with Tarapacá in the dossier under the heading "the northern courts' non-recognition of trans women as women," reflecting the shared judicial geography of northern Chile. However, the specific Iquique Court of Appeals annulment was delivered in Tarapacá, and Arica's own data contribution is limited to a 0.84 % share of national cases (2024). No trans-specific incident, court ruling, or enforcement failure originating in Arica was identified. The deviation below national rests on the shared northern judicial-climate framing and the broader pattern — reported for both the 2024 and 2025 Movilh annual surveys — that homo/transphobia cases rose in most regions outside the metropolitan core.

Against the national 0.72, this is a −0.03 deviation, the smallest in the scored set. Compared with Tarapacá (0.64), Arica is 0.05 higher because it lacks the concrete femicide-annulment ruling; the northern-court context applies but is not evidenced with a named local finding. Compared with Ñuble (0.67), Arica is 0.02 higher: Ñuble's +300 % surge is a more specific and dramatic statistical signal than Arica's sub-percent case share.

For a visitor, the practical exposure in Arica is not materially different from the national baseline; the small deduction reflects the dossier's explicit grouping under "worse than national" and the absence of any positive institutional finding (no diversity office, no municipal ordinance, no documented court protection).

sources.claim: Chilevisión crime report: the Court of Appeals of Iquique annulled the entire trial over the killing of a transgender woman after holding that Chile's "femicide" offence protects only "a person biologically female," so the conviction could not stand as framed — a northern-court finding that the country's strongest gendered-violence protection does not extend to trans women. The dossier cites it as the basis for grouping Tarapacá and Arica y Parinacota as worse-than-national on shared judicial geography; the ruling itself is Tarapacá's.

Movilh's XXIII Annual Human-Rights Report on Sexual and Gender Diversity (2024 data, published March 2025), full per-region table: 2,847 recorded cases nationally (+78.7 %), with Arica y Parinacota holding a 0.84 % share — among the lowest in the country — in a year that saw increases in 11 of 16 regions; small-share regions where a single case dominates the rate.

sources.title: Las denuncias por casos de discriminación a comunidad LGTBIQ+ aumentan en Arica y Parinacota
sources.claim: Movilh's annual rights report covering 2021 (published April 2022) showed Chile-wide homophobia/transphobia complaints and cases falling 12%, the first drop in eight years, but in five regions they rose and Arica y Parinacota was one of them: its reports climbed around 300% against 2020. The piece ties the national decline to the visibility won by the sexual-diversity movement in the year equal marriage was approved (2021). For this record it evidences the region's own complaint trajectory running against the national trend — concrete regional data backing the dossier's grouping of the northern regions as worse than national.

sources.title: Arica se convierte en el cuarto territorio donde Iguales presta apoyo legal gratuito en casos de discriminación por orientación sexual y/o identidad de género
sources.claim: On 14 November 2017 Fundación Iguales announced that Arica became the fourth territory where it provides free legal aid for discrimination cases based on sexual orientation and/or gender identity, via a collaboration agreement with pro-bono lawyer Piera Balbontin Nef covering Arica's jurisdiction. The foundation's legal director said discrimination is greater in regions far from the capital, which is why local legal support matters. For this record it documents that an accessible local channel for anti-LGBTI discrimination complaints exists in the region itself — a concrete mitigation resource for a visitor facing an incident, complementing the national anti-discrimination framework.
